title: Derived ringed-topos pullback preserves compatible central scalars
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi, where $A$ and $B$ are sheaves of commutative unital rings, presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Suppose given unital homomorphisms $s_A:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,A)$ and $s_B:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal D,B)$ such that the structural map $c:u^{-1}A\to B$ carries $u^{-1}s_A(r)$ to $s_B(r)$ for every $r\in R$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] define $(r f)_U(x)=s_A(r)|_U f_U(x)$, and likewise using $s_B$. Equip the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(A),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with the induced $R$-linear structures [def-weil-linear-category, lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. The canonical K-flat derived pullback $Lu^*:D(A)\to D(B)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor]. In particular it sends the endomorphism induced by the actual scalar section $s_A(r)$ to that induced by $s_B(r)$; no flatness of $c$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), K-flat computation and exactness. The compatible-central-scalar assertion is the implicit compatible-central-scalar prerequisite, not a separately stated clause of 06YY.

proof.text: Use the existing Hom-module action restricted along s_A and s_B. For an A-module M and scalar r, take the generalized test sheaf T=|M|, the constant arrow a:T→|A| defined by s_A(r), the identity b:T→|M|, and the scalar endomorphism t. Apply the moduleSMul graph equation of the algebraic inverse-image presentation. Evaluate at the image of any section m of I(M) under the underlying-sheaf isomorphism. Naturality and the inverse-isomorphism identity give I(mu_M(r))(m)=k m for k=e_A(L(a)(x)). The structural-map compatibility and hs give c(k)=s_B(r).

For change of rings use the sheafification adjunction to test equality of its endomorphisms on the presheaf tensor product. Naturality of the adjunction unit identifies the induced endomorphism with the map id tensor I(mu_M(r)). Sectionwise extension-of-scalars Hom extensionality reduces to tensors 1 tensor m. Step 1 and balancing give 1 tensor (k m)=c(k)(1 tensor m)=s_B(r)(1 tensor m). The unit is B-linear, so sheafification preserves this identity. Transport through the object-identification isomorphisms hobj and use hmap to obtain uStar(mu_M(r))=mu_uStar(M)(r). Mathlib Functor.linear_iff gives linearity of ordinary pullback.

Apply the existing exact derived-pullback theorem to obtain its exact realization LF0 and comparison epsilon0. The universal property of the supplied LF,epsilon identifies LF with LF0 by the natural isomorphism Functor.leftDerivedUnique. Exactness makes LF0 additive, and additivity transports across this natural isomorphism. This uses the existing K-flat construction as a theorem and does not construct any additional resolutions.

For each r compare natural endomorphisms gamma1(X)=LF(r id_X) and gamma2(X)=r id_LF(X) of LF. Bilinearity in the source and target proves their naturality. By the left-derived universal property (Mathlib Functor.leftDerived_ext), they agree if their precompositions with Qh agree after epsilon. Naturality of epsilon at r id_Y gives this equality: Qh and ordinary pullback on homotopy categories are linear, so both sides reduce to r times epsilon_Y. Thus LF preserves scalar identities on every derived object directly. Functor.linear_iff gives full scalar linearity; combine with step 3 for the additive linear-functor assertion.

Statement change: it now says A and B are sheaves of commutative unital rings. This does not weaken anything. The cited Lu^* node (lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback), lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product and Stacks conventions section-algebra all assume commutative rings. The report's M_2(k) counterexample checks out: with e_11 as scalar, right multiplication by e_12 times the scalar is not A-linear (e_21 gives 0 against e_22). The only citer, the Q05 reduction-tower functor, applies it to commutative O_E coefficient sheaves. Step 1: multiplication by s_A(r) is A-linear by commutativity, and composition is bilinear. Step 2: the algebraic inverse image carries multiplication by s_A(r) to multiplication by u^{-1}s_A(r) (its scalar-multiplication graph condition). Tensor balancing with the hypothesis on c is checked on pure tensors, then sums, then sheafification. Step 3: naturality of epsilon on K(A) at mu_P, with Q R-linear (mathlib leaf); cancelling the invertible epsilon_P is correct, and the directions match the node. Step 4: conjugation by Q(p) for a K-flat resolution P->K with flat terms. Step 5: scalar preservation for every derived morphism, plus additivity from exactness (definition of exact functor). Edge cases: r=0,1, zero ring, identity morphism, Z->F_2 on a point. Sources: 06YY = sites-cohomology lemma-derived-base-change (line 3585), 06YS, 03D6; no SGA. The DAG scan found no duplicate.
